name: BarChart
intent: Values side by side as bars, one group or stack per category, like invoices by status for each week. Bars stand up, or run across with orientation horizontal.
usage: Use BarChart to compare amounts across categories or periods. It is one component: pass categories and series. orientation vertical puts the categories along the bottom with bars standing up; horizontal lists them down the start with bars running across, best for long names or ranked lists like top customers. Bars sit side by side per category, or on top of each other with stacked, so the bar height is the total and the colors are its parts. barWidth thin draws 8px bars with rounded ends, for a long run of periods like a month of daily use. showValues writes each value at the end of its bar. On an upright chart, a grant, limit or target goes in referenceLines, a dashed line across the chart with its label and value at the end, drawn over the bars so it stays visible where they pass it; give that line values, one level per category, when it changes during the period and it steps instead. A forecast stays in the same series: projectedFrom names its first forecast category, and its bars draw see-through from there. marker draws a thin line down the chart at one category, like Today. A horizontal chart ignores all three. Hover or use the arrow keys for a tooltip with every series in that category. animate lets bars grow out from the baseline. Put the chart's title and report link in the Section or Card around it. ChartIntent: green | olive | cyan | orange | pink | gray | purple | yellow | red | mint (the kit category colors). title and subtitle write a heading over the chart; showHeader turns it off when the Card around it already says the same. highlight picks out one or more bars in the highlight intent, like the biggest and smallest in a ranked list. The keys under the chart are the kit Legend; legendPosition moves them over it or beside it. See contracts/barchart.json for the full contract. A legend beside the chart drops under it when the chart's own box is narrower than 360px.

label.note: Names the chart for screen readers and captions its data table, like Revenue by period.

title.note: Visible title over the chart, like Revenue by period. The screen-reader name still comes from label.

subtitle.note: A quieter line under the title, like Last 12 months, all accounts.

showHeader.note: Shows the title and subtitle. Off draws the chart alone, when the Card or Section around it already carries the title.

categories.note: The category labels: along the bottom when vertical (they thin out when they would overlap), down the start when horizontal (long ones shorten with an ellipsis; the tooltip shows the full name).

series.itemShape: { name: string; values: number[]; intent?: ChartIntent; projectedFrom?: number }
series.note: One entry per line or bar color, with one value per category. intent picks the color; by default series take green, olive, cyan, orange, pink, gray, then purple, yellow, red and mint. projectedFrom (upright charts) is the first category that is a forecast, counted from 0: its bars and the ones after it draw see-through in the same color, and the tooltip and table say projected.

orientation.note: vertical: categories along the bottom, bars standing up. horizontal: categories down the start, bars running across, values along the bottom.

highlight.note: Category numbers to pick out, counted from 0, like the top and bottom of a ranked chart. They take the highlight intent instead of their series color.

stacked.note: Piles the series in one bar per category; the bar height is the total.

barWidth.note: wide: bars fill most of their category's space, with square corners. thin: every bar is 8px, like a medium Meter bar, with its rounded ends; a stack rounds only its two outer ends. For long runs of periods, like a month of days. Pointing anywhere in a category still shows its tooltip.

showValues.note: The short value at the end of each bar (side-by-side bars) or each stack: above it when vertical, past it when horizontal.

showGrid.note: Faint lines at each value tick.

showLegend.note: Colored squares with the series names under the chart.

legendPosition.note: Where the keys sit: under the chart, over it, or in a column beside it.

animate.note: Subtle motion when the chart appears. Off draws it at once. Always off when the person prefers reduced motion.

format.note: How values read. Axis ticks and value labels are short ($4.2M, 750K); the tooltip and table show the full number.

height.note: Height of the drawing in px, axis labels included. Vertical defaults to 240. Horizontal grows by 36 a category unless you set it. The width fills the container.

emptyLabel.note: Shown when there are no categories or series.

referenceLines.itemShape: { value: number; label: string; intent?: ChartIntent; values?: number[] }
referenceLines.note: Upright charts only. Dashed lines across the chart at a value, like a grant, a limit or a target, drawn over the bars so they stay visible where the bars pass them. label names it, like Grant; the chart writes the short value after it, at the end of the line, clear of the bars. Neutral gray unless intent picks a color. The scale always reaches the highest line. values gives one level per category for a limit that changes during the period, like a grant a top-up raises: the line steps on the category it changed, and the label reports the level it ends at.

marker.note: Upright charts only. A thin line down the chart at one category, counted from 0, with its label over the top, like Today.

useWhen: Comparing amounts across categories or periods.
Parts of a total per period, with stacked.
Long category names or a ranked list, like top customers by balance, with orientation horizontal.
A ranked list where one or two bars matter most: sort the data and pick them out with highlight.
A long run of periods, like usage per day for a month, with barWidth thin so the bars read as a light rhythm.
Usage against a grant or limit over a period, like credits used by day against the grant: referenceLines, with values when the grant steps up partway.
Actual and forecast periods in one run of bars: projectedFrom on the series, with a marker at today.
doNot: Do not use it for a long, smooth trend. Use LineChart.
Do not use it for one share of a total. Use PieChart.
Do not draw charts with loose SVG or a chart library. Use the kit charts.
Do not use raw hex; pick an intent.
Do not use highlight on every bar; pick out one or two, or use a series intent.
Do not use barWidth thin for a handful of categories; the bars get lost in wide bands. Keep wide.
Do not fake a limit or target with an extra series. It shows in the legend, the tooltip and the table as data. Use referenceLines.
Do not draw forecast bars as a second series in a lighter color. Use projectedFrom, so actual and forecast stay one series with one name.
Do not fake a changing limit with several flat reference lines. Give the one line its values per category.
Do not use referenceLines, marker or projectedFrom on a horizontal chart; they belong to a time axis and a horizontal chart ignores them.
a11y: A figure named by label. The drawing is hidden from screen readers; a visually hidden table holds every value, with the categories as rows and the series as columns.
The chart takes focus: the arrow keys (and Home and End) move through the categories, in either orientation, and show the same tooltip as pointing at them. Escape hides it.
Colors come with a legend and the tooltip names each series, so color is not the only way to tell them apart.

Reference lines and the marker are listed after the table for screen readers, like Grant: 1,150 and Today: Sep 23; a line that steps reports both ends, like Grant: 1,150 to 1,750. Forecast values say projected in the tooltip and the table.
Motion is subtle and optional (animate), and never plays when the person prefers reduced motion.
snippet:
<BarChart
  label="Invoices by status by time"
  categories={weeks}
  series={[
    { name: "Current", values: current, intent: "pink" },
    { name: "Paid", values: paid, intent: "green" },
  ]}
  format="currency"
  stacked
/>
